title: Subset Sum Predicate
content: **IsSubsetSum A n**: Asserts that $n$ can be expressed as a sum of distinct elements from $A$. Formally, $\exists B \subseteq A, \sum_{b \in B} b = n$, where the sum uses `Finset.sum id`. This is the fundamental predicate: a set $A$ represents $n$ iff `IsSubsetSum A n` holds. The subset sum problem ($\exists B \subseteq A$ with prescribed sum) is NP-complete in general.
mathContext: $\text{IsSubsetSum}(A, n) \iff \exists B \subseteq A : \sum_{b \in B} b = n$

title: Non-Representing Predicate
content: **NonRepresenting A n**: The negation of `IsSubsetSum`—no subset of $A$ sums to $n$. This is the avoidance condition central to Problem #361. The set of non-representing sets for a fixed $n$ forms a downward-closed family (an ideal in the inclusion order), since removing elements from $A$ cannot create new subset sums.

title: Maximum Non-Representing Size
content: **maxNonReprSize c n**: The maximum cardinality of a non-representing subset of $\{1, \ldots, \lfloor cn \rfloor\}$. Computed as $\sup\{|B| : B \in \mathcal{P}(\{1,\ldots,\lfloor cn \rfloor\}),\; \text{NonRepresenting}(B, n)\}$ via `Finset.powerset.filter.sup`. This is the extremal function that Problem #361 asks to estimate. Noncomputable since it involves filtering over an exponentially large powerset.

title: Irregularity Conjecture
content: **ErdosProblem361**: States that for every $c > 0$, the function $n \mapsto \text{maxNonReprSize}(c, n)$ is not monotone. This formalizes the irregularity question: the arithmetic structure of $n$ causes the maximum to fluctuate, rather than growing steadily. Defined as $\forall c > 0, \neg \text{Monotone}(\lambda n.\, \text{maxNonReprSize}(c, n))$.
mathContext: $\forall c > 0, n \mapsto \max\{|A| : A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,\lfloor cn \rfloor\}, n \notin \Sigma(A)\}$ is non-monotone

title: Plausible Θ(√n) Growth
content: **maxNonRepr_plausible_theta**: Axiomatizes the plausible conjecture that $\text{maxNonReprSize}(c, n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$ using Mathlib's `Asymptotics.IsTheta`. The $\sqrt{n}$ threshold emerges because a $k$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,cn\}$ can form $O(2^k)$ distinct sums, and when $k \approx \sqrt{n}$ the sum space saturates the range $[0, n]$, making avoidance of any particular target nearly impossible.

title: Empty Set is Non-Representing
content: **nonRepresenting_empty**: For $n > 0$, the empty set $\emptyset$ is non-representing. The only subset of $\emptyset$ is $\emptyset$ itself, which sums to 0, and $0 \neq n$ when $n > 0$. Proved by assuming a witnessing subset $B \subseteq \emptyset$, showing $B = \emptyset$, and deriving a contradiction via `omega`.

title: Subset Monotonicity
content: **nonRepresenting_subset**: If $B$ is non-representing and $A \subseteq B$, then $A$ is also non-representing. Every subset of $A$ is also a subset of $B$ (by transitivity of $\subseteq$), so if no subset of $B$ sums to $n$, then no subset of $A$ does either. This establishes that `NonRepresenting` is a downward-closed property.

title: Singleton {1} is Non-Representing for n ≥ 2
content: **singleton_one_nonRepr**: For $n \geq 2$, the set $\{1\}$ does not represent $n$. The subsets of $\{1\}$ are $\emptyset$ (sum 0) and $\{1\}$ (sum 1), neither of which equals $n \geq 2$. Proved by case analysis on `Finset.subset_singleton_iff` and `omega`. This provides a concrete witness that $\text{maxNonReprSize}(c, n) \geq 1$ when $c \geq 1/n$.

title: Small-c Regime
content: **maxNonRepr_large_n**: For $c < 1$ and sufficiently large $n$, $\text{maxNonReprSize}(c, n) = \lfloor cn \rfloor$—the maximum is the entire set. This holds because $\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor cn \rfloor} i = \lfloor cn \rfloor(\lfloor cn \rfloor + 1)/2 < n$ when $c < 1$ and $n$ is large, so no subset can sum to $n$. Sorried; the proof would use the triangular number formula and asymptotic comparison.
